nodes.name: cyclin dependent kinase 6
nodes.description: CDK6 is a serine/threonine kinase that phosphorylates the retinoblastoma protein to promote G1/S cell cycle transition and is overexpressed in multiple cancer types including lymphomas and solid tumors.

nodes.name: cyclin dependent kinase 4
nodes.description: CDK4 is a serine/threonine kinase that phosphorylates the retinoblastoma protein to promote G1/S cell cycle transition and is frequently dysregulated in cancer through amplification or overexpression.

nodes.name: B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase
nodes.description: BRAF encodes a serine/threonine protein kinase that phosphorylates MEK1/2 in the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway and is frequently mutated in melanoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma, and other cancers.
nodes.name_id: b raf proto oncogene serine threonine kinase

nodes.name: kinase inhibition
nodes.description: CDK4/6 kinase inhibition

nodes.name: enzyme inhibition
nodes.description: Enzyme inhibition reduces the catalytic activity of a target protein by blocking its active site or allosteric regulatory regions, thereby decreasing the formation of downstream metabolic products or signaling molecules relevant to disease pathology.

nodes.name: Neutrophil degranulation
nodes.description: Neutrophil degranulation is the process by which activated neutrophils release the contents of their cytoplasmic granules, including proteases, antimicrobial peptides, and reactive oxygen species, into the extracellular space or phagolysosome to eliminate pathogens and damaged tissue.

nodes.name: Ub-specific processing proteases
nodes.description: Ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs) cleave polyubiquitin chains and remove ubiquitin moieties from substrate proteins to regulate protein stability, localization, and function.

nodes.name: Interleukin-4 and Interleukin-13 signaling
nodes.description: Interleukin-4 and Interleukin-13 signaling activates STAT6 through Type II cytokine receptors to promote T helper 2 cell differentiation, alternative macrophage activation, and immunoglobulin class switching to IgE and IgG4.

nodes.name: Neddylation
nodes.description: Neddylation is the post-translational conjugation of NEDD8 ubiquitin-like protein to cullin proteins, which activates cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase complexes to promote polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of target proteins.

nodes.name: Separation of Sister Chromatids
nodes.description: Sister chromatids separate at the centromere during anaphase when cohesin proteins are cleaved by separase, allowing each chromatid to migrate to opposite poles of the dividing cell.

nodes.name: Amplification  of signal from unattached  kinetochores via a MAD2  inhibitory signal
nodes.description: Unattached kinetochores activate MAD2-mediated inhibition of the anaphase-promoting complex to prevent mitotic progression until chromosomal attachment is complete.
nodes.name_id: amplification of signal from unattached kinetochores via a mad2 inhibitory signal

nodes.name: EML4 and NUDC in mitotic spindle formation
nodes.description: EML4 and NUDC proteins cooperatively nucleate and stabilize microtubule minus ends at spindle poles during mitosis through their interaction with the γ-tubulin ring complex.
nodes.name_id: eml4 and nudc in mitotic spindle formation

nodes.name: RHO GTPases Activate Formins
nodes.description: RHO GTPases in their active GTP-bound state directly bind to and activate formin proteins, which nucleate and processively elongate unbranched actin filaments.

nodes.name: Resolution of Sister Chromatid Cohesion
nodes.description: Sister chromatid cohesion is resolved through proteolytic cleavage of cohesin complexes by separase during anaphase, allowing replicated chromosomes to segregate to opposite poles of the dividing cell.

nodes.name: Mitotic Prometaphase
nodes.description: During mitotic prometaphase, the nuclear envelope disassembles, kinetochores assemble at centromeres, and spindle microtubules attach to chromosomes to begin their segregation toward opposite poles of the cell.

nodes.name: Regulation of PLK1 Activity at G2/M Transition
nodes.description: PLK1 is activated by CDK1-cyclin B1 phosphorylation during G2/M phase and subsequently phosphorylates CDC25C to promote mitotic entry through positive feedback amplification of CDK1 activity.
nodes.name_id: regulation of plk1 activity at g2 m transition

nodes.name: The role of GTSE1 in G2/M progression after G2 checkpoint
nodes.description: GTSE1 promotes G2/M phase transition by antagonizing p53-mediated cell cycle arrest at the G2 checkpoint, allowing cells with DNA damage to proceed through mitosis.
nodes.name_id: the role of gtse1 in g2 m progression after g2 checkpoint

nodes.name: Cyclin A/B1/B2 associated events during G2/M transition
nodes.description: Cyclin A, B1, and B2 sequentially activate CDK1 to drive G2/M phase transition through phosphorylation of nuclear lamins, histone H1, and checkpoint proteins, enabling nuclear envelope breakdown and mitotic spindle formation.
nodes.name_id: cyclin a b1 b2 associated events during g2 m transition

nodes.name: Cyclin A:Cdk2-associated events at S phase entry
nodes.description: Cyclin A-Cdk2 complexes phosphorylate substrates required for DNA replication initiation and S phase progression, including Cdc6 and geminin, to promote origin firing and prevent re-replication.
nodes.name_id: cyclin a cdk2 associated events at s phase entry

nodes.name: Condensation of Prophase Chromosomes
nodes.description: During prophase, chromatin fibers progressively coil and compact through hierarchical organization of nucleosomes and higher-order structures, transforming diffuse chromatin into visible condensed chromosomes that are approximately 10,000-fold more compact than interphase chromatin.

nodes.name: Oxidative Stress Induced Senescence
nodes.description: Accumulation of reactive oxygen species damages cellular macromolecules, triggers DNA damage responses, and activates p53-p21 signaling to enforce irreversible cell cycle arrest characteristic of senescence.

nodes.name: Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (SASP)
nodes.description: Senescent cells secrete pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and proteases that promote tissue inflammation, remodel the extracellular matrix, and alter the microenvironment to drive aging-related pathology and cancer progression.

nodes.name: SUMOylation of DNA replication proteins
nodes.description: SUMOylation of DNA replication proteins involves the covalent attachment of Small Ubiquitin-like Modifier (SUMO) proteins to lysine residues on replication machinery components, regulating their stability, localization, and interaction with other proteins during DNA synthesis.

nodes.name: Regulation of TP53 Activity through Phosphorylation
nodes.description: ATM and CHK2 kinases phosphorylate TP53 at serine 15 in response to DNA damage, preventing MDM2-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thereby stabilizing and activating TP53 as a transcription factor.
nodes.name_id: regulation of tp53 activity through phosphorylation

nodes.name: Regulation of APC/C activators between G1/S and early anaphase
nodes.description: The APC/C is activated by Cdc20 during mitosis and by Cdh1 during G1 phase, with Cdc20 activity restricted to mitosis through phosphorylation-dependent regulation and Cdh1 activation occurring after APC/C-Cdc20 inactivation to maintain G1 arrest.
nodes.name_id: regulation of apc c activators between g1 s and early anaphase

nodes.name: Regulation of MITF-M-dependent genes involved in cell cycle and proliferation
nodes.description: MITF-M transcription factor regulates expression of genes controlling G1/S phase progression and cellular proliferation in melanocytic lineage cells.
nodes.name_id: regulation of mitf m dependent genes involved in cell cycle and proliferation

nodes.name: Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC) Disassembly
nodes.description: Nuclear pore complexes disassemble during mitosis through phosphorylation-dependent removal of nucleoporin components from the nuclear envelope, allowing chromosome segregation and reformation of daughter cell nuclei.

nodes.name: Activation of NIMA Kinases NEK9, NEK6, NEK7
nodes.description: NEK9 autophosphorylation at the centrosome triggers its activation and subsequent phosphorylation of downstream kinases NEK6 and NEK7, which collectively regulate mitotic spindle assembly and checkpoint control.
nodes.name_id: activation of nima kinases nek9 nek6 nek7

nodes.name: G2/M DNA replication checkpoint
nodes.description: The G2/M DNA replication checkpoint halts cell cycle progression at the G2/M transition until DNA damage is repaired or replication is complete, primarily through ATM/ATR-mediated p53 activation and p21-induced CDK inhibition.

nodes.name: Golgi Cisternae Pericentriolar Stack Reorganization
nodes.description: Golgi cisternae undergo dynamic reorganization and repositioning around the centrosome during the cell cycle, involving cisternal unstacking, lateral dispersal, and reassembly into a compact pericentriolar stack through microtubule-dependent transport and tethering factor interactions.

nodes.name: TP53 Regulates Transcription of Genes Involved in G2 Cell Cycle Arrest
nodes.description: TP53 protein binds to DNA response elements and activates transcription of CDK inhibitor genes including CDKN1A, which inhibits cyclin-dependent kinase complexes to prevent G2/M phase transition.
nodes.name_id: tp53 regulates transcription of genes involved in g2 cell cycle arrest

nodes.name: Phosphorylation of Emi1
nodes.description: Emi1 is phosphorylated by cyclin-CDK complexes during S and G2 phases of the cell cycle, leading to its ubiquitin-mediated degradation and allowing APC/C activation.

nodes.name: Phosphorylation of the APC/C
nodes.description: The anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) undergoes phosphorylation by cyclin-dependent kinases and polo-like kinases, which enhances its ubiquitin ligase activity and promotes the degradation of cyclins and securin during cell cycle progression.

nodes.name: AURKA Activation by TPX2
nodes.description: TPX2 binds to and activates Aurora Kinase A (AURKA) through relief of autoinhibition, enabling AURKA to phosphorylate downstream substrates including NUSAP1 and KIF11 to promote mitotic spindle assembly and chromosome segregation.

nodes.name: APC/C:Cdc20 mediated degradation of Cyclin B

alternate_pathway_names.R-HSA-174184: Cdc20:Phospho-APC/C mediated degradation of Cyclin A

nodes.description: APC/C bound to Cdc20 ubiquitinates Cyclin B at the metaphase-anaphase transition, targeting it for proteasomal degradation and enabling mitotic exit.
nodes.name_id: apc c cdc20 mediated degradation of cyclin b

nodes.name: Antigen processing: Ubiquitination & Proteasome degradation
nodes.description: Ubiquitinated proteins are recognized by the 26S proteasome, which cleaves them into peptides that are loaded onto MHC class I molecules in the endoplasmic reticulum for presentation to CD8+ T cells.

nodes.name: Processing of DNA double-strand break ends
nodes.description: DNA double-strand break ends are processed through 5' to 3' exonuclease activity and nucleotide addition to generate compatible overhangs for ligation or homologous recombination repair.
nodes.name_id: processing of dna double strand break ends

nodes.name: Estrogen-dependent gene expression
nodes.description: Estrogen binds to estrogen receptors in the cytoplasm or nucleus, which then translocate to or bind estrogen response elements in DNA to recruit coactivators and modulate transcription of target genes including those regulating cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis.

nodes.name: DNA Damage/Telomere Stress Induced Senescence
nodes.description: Persistent DNA damage or critically shortened telomeres activate p53 and p16/Rb pathways, triggering irreversible cell cycle arrest and senescence through CDK inhibition.
nodes.name_id: dna damage telomere stress induced senescence
